[[New Edubiase United FC|New Edubiase]] (8) | longest losses = [[New Edubiase United FC|New Edubiase]] (6) | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2015 Ghanaian Premier League|2015]] | nextseason = [[2017 Ghanaian Premier League|2017]] | updated = 18 September 2016 }} The '''2016 [[Ghanaian Premier League]]''' was the 60th season of top professional [[association football]] in [[Ghana]]. The domestic league season began on 21 January and concluded on 18 September with [[All Stars F.C.|Wa All Stars]] winning their first league title. Only the games between Asante Kotoko and the Hearts of Oak attracted a high attendance.{{Cite web|url=https://mobile.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/SportsArchive/Low-Stadium-Attendance-in-Ghana-because-of-European-Leagues-182232|title=Low Stadium Attendance in Ghana because of European Leagues|website=mobile.ghanaweb.com|access-date=2018-06-05}} ==Teams== The [[Ghanaian Premier League]] comprises 16 sides, of which the bottom three - [[Sekondi Hasaacas F.C.|Hasaacas]], [[New Edubiase United FC|New Edubiase]] and Techiman City - will be relegated to the [[Ghana Football Leagues|Division One]]. In December 2016, Dreams FC was demoted from the Ghana Premier League due to an anomaly with the registration of a player.
